name: link-field
title: Link field
description: A link as a CMS stores it: the text, where it goes and whether it opens a new tab, with the address checked, recognised in words and made safe.
docs: value and onValueChange speak { text, href, newTab, rel }: text is trimmed, href is the destination as it is stored, empty while the destination is refused or not a link yet, so a refused address is never reported or submitted, newTab is false for a kind of link that cannot open in a new tab, and rel is "noopener noreferrer" for an external link that does, so the page it opens cannot reach back into yours. The second argument says whether the link is usable: a recognised destination of an allowed kind and, with requireText, some text. The destination takes a web address, a path ("/pricing"), an anchor ("#faq"), mailto: and tel: links, and the bare forms of them: northwind.example/pricing gets https:// in front, ines@orbit.example becomes mailto:, +31 20 555 0142 becomes tel:+31205550142. It says in words which kind it recognised (a line under the field and a matching icon in front of it), and refuses what could harm a visitor: javascript:, data:, file: and other schemes, and a path that starts with two slashes, or with a slash and a backslash. allow limits the kinds (external, relative, anchor, email, phone) and a destination of another kind is explained in words. Messages for what is wrong wait until a field is left (and until a press is over, so a submit is not swallowed) and then follow the typing; the line under the destination always has one line of room, so nothing jumps. The checkbox is disabled, with a line saying why, for anchors, emails and phone links. The preview is the link as a button, with a small arrow when it leaves the site in a new tab. label and hideLabel name the group (a fieldset), name adds hidden inputs <name>-text, <name>-href, <name>-new-tab and <name>-rel, disabled disables every control, and labels renames every phrase.
